slides.texte_overlay:
How to walk into any room
like you belong there
Walk in at a normal pace. Not rushing, not hesitating. A steady walk tells everyone you're comfortable wherever you are.
Keep your hands relaxed and visible. Out of your pockets, not crossed. Open hands make you look calm and approachable.
Make eye contact with someone in the first seconds. A small nod or smile. It breaks the tension and shows confidence.
Know one thing to say. "How do you know the host?" or "This place is great." An easy first line removes the fear of the first conversation.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. Knowing interesting things makes you feel at home in any conversation.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Knowing interesting things makes you feel at home in any conversation.

slides.texte_overlay: Dress one level above the occasion. Slightly sharper clothes make you feel more confident as soon as you walk in. Small effort, big effect.
Remember everyone is thinking about themselves. Nobody is judging your entrance as much as you think. Relax and enjoy it.
